Bridger, Heather, Thaxter, Roberts, Doubleday, Snell, and others, supporting Bert Clayton, our Eastleigh member, who may win the individual title, is certainly a team of possibilities.

Jock Martin, a stalwart for many years in this race, was indisposed, as was also Fred Rickards. Readman and Roberts were also prevented from entering and we could only muster six entries against last year's eleven.

Clayton, Heather, Roberts, Thaxter, Doubleday, Bridger, Goold, Elliott, East, Snell and others have great potentialities, and with conscientious, steady training, we may expect a team which will represent the Club with credit.

Bert Clayton immediately went into the lead, accompanied by Bert East, with Syd Roberts leading the rest in pursuit. After a small lap of the Common, Clayton was still leading, Eddie Heather having worked his way into second place.

Our "B" team (Clark, Doubleday, Roberts and True) managed to get in the prize-winners again, taking second handicap team prize. Brunning, Jones and Little also gave us encouraging performances, and their constant support of open races is an excellent testimony to their keenness and club-spirit.
Roberts, Doubleday, Clark and Heather, of the "B" team, walked well and comprised the second handicap team. Eddie Heather's forward walking, his best to date, earned third individual handicap prize.

Charles set off up Dale Hill in his indominatable manner and ran a well judged race throughout, shaking off the persistent Roberts of TVH. Unfortunately the S.L.H. boy, Barber, was in full cry and forced Charles back into 7th place despite the encouragement of our supporters.

Roberts (SLH) got away right from the start and it was soon evident that John Thresher would be second. Tony Fairclough,although still below peak,was third until the last mile when he was overhauled by a fast finishing trio,but was well pleased with the result - as indeed was Dabbs who was surprised…

After one lap he was still in the twenties and although he began to make ground on the second circuit it was a slow and painful business against such opposition as Adcocks and Kilby (Coventry), Rose, Wheeler and Wyatt (New Zealand), Tulloh, Roberts and Barlow.

Once again the leading pack slowed up and Roberts (SLH) took the initiative with Bob Holt (Hercules) and Robinson (Achilles) close behind. With all this chopping and changing the inevitable happened and unhappily, Mick Gowan (HHH) was badly spiked and had to drop out.

Thresher passed Roberts down the finishing straight, only for Tulloh to pass them both and break the tape. With Bob Holt of Hercules also closing fast, only 11 seconds separated the first four at the finish.
Whitley (TVH), an unknown quantity, set off 35 seconds ahead of Gerry, with Tulloh (Ports) 1:58 further behind, followed by Barton (Windsor) and Roberts (SLH).
S.L.H. proved to be a surprise package here for, without Roberts and Gilson, they led us until the final stages of the last leg when Laurie O'Hara did his usual duty for us.
